sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Digital Advertising Media Arbitrage and Affiliate Lead Gen

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg Double Tax Treaty Network, including DTA with the United States and DTA with the People's Republic of China
Luxembourg Bilateral Investment Treaty network administered by the Ministry of the Economy
EU free movement of establishment and capital under the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union
Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty-Related Measures to Prevent Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (MLI)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners ('RBE Law'); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019 on the practical organisation of the RBE; Law of 17 December 2021 and Law of 25 March 2020 implementing the EU AML/CFT package; CSSF Regulation 12-02 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Articles of Association of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Trade/Companies Registrar of the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if HCCH 1961 Contracting State) OR Consular Legalization by the competent Luxembourg Embassy/Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Non-Dissolution of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the jurisdiction of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity card of each individual ultimate beneficial owner and each director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing Passport Authority / National ID Bureau of the beneficial owner's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy followed by Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address for each individual UBO, director and authorised signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Municipal registration office, utility provider or established financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized attestation or apostilled/consular legalized official certificate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter / AML due-diligence letter for the entity and principal shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed bank of the shareholder or beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization where required by the Luxembourg notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, UBOs, shareholders and authorized signatories against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, FATF High-Risk Jurisdictions lists, and Luxembourg national asset-freeze measures maintained by the Ministry of Finance. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for politically exposed persons ('PEPs'); enhanced ongoing transaction monitoring, source-of-funds verification, and annual re-screening are required for the medium-risk enhanced AML profile applicable to affiliate media-buying entities.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), integrated with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) – https://www.lbr.lu/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names may be expressed in French, German, Luxembourgish, or another language using the Latin alphabet; the name must include the statutory legal-form identifier 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL'. Names in non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into a Latin-alphabet rendering approved by the Luxembourg notary and RCS. The name must not violate public order, must not be misleading, and must clearly distinguish the entity from existing registered names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS rejects a proposed name, the applicant may first submit a written request for registry review within 15 days of the refusal notification. If review is unsuccessful, an administrative appeal may be lodged with the Luxembourg Administrative Tribunal within one month of the rejection notice; legal representation by a Luxembourg avocat is mandatory. The name reservation may be renewed by filing a fresh availability request before the initial 30-day window expires, subject to continued availability of the name and RCS policy.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Pure virtual mailbox offices are not accepted as a statutory registered office. Luxembourg requires a genuine physical address in Luxembourg where central administration and statutory books are kept. Approved commercial domiciliation arrangements with a physical presence, resident representative and correspondence handling services are permissible for the SARL, provided the entity maintains verifiable operational substance and local governance records.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 15–20% annual probability for this Medium_Risk_Enhanced profile; unannounced registry, AML supervisor, and tax administration inspections become materially more likely if a virtual/domiciliation office is used, if UBO documentation is incomplete, or if high transaction volumes from affiliate media buying are observed without adequate commercial substance.

Apostille or consular legalization of foreign corporate, identity, address and bank reference documents (bundle of 4 documents)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of legalized corporate documents into French and/or German
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg registered court translator / sworn translator

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office and physical domiciliation agreement, first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark for regulated Luxembourg domiciliation agents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market fee for a specialised corporate due-diligence memorandum

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as consolidated and amended; SARL regime at Articles 710-1 to 710-25; complemented by the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and Companies, and the Law of 1 March 2013 on the dematerialisation of the register.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg-Kirchberg; electronic filing portal via guichet.lu and rcs.lbr.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte constitutif) containing the Statuts constitutifs (Articles of Association), followed by mandatory inscription with the RCS and publication in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital is EUR 12,000 for a SARL (Article 710-1). The full capital must be subscribed and paid up in cash or in kind at incorporation. Cash contributions are held in a blocked escrow account with a Luxembourg credit institution and must be evidenced by a banker's certificate delivered to the notary; in-kind contributions require a report of the réviseur d'entreprises agréé (approved statutory auditor).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the share capital of the Company, fixed at EUR 12,000 divided into ordinary shares, is hereby subscribed in full by the founding members as set out in the subscription schedule appended hereto, and that each respective contribution is satisfied by transfer of funds evidenced by the banker's certificate. RESOLVED further, that the registered office is hereby established at the address identified in the Articles of Association, to be effective upon incorporation, and the Manager is directed to procure the registration thereof with the Luxembourg Business Registers. RESOLVED further, that [Name] is appointed Manager of the Company for an unlimited term, acting alone (signature individuelle), with authority to open and operate bank accounts, appoint professional advisers, and carry out all steps to complete incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) online search module and the Luxembourg Intellectual Property Office for trade mark search
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders run a conflict search against the RCS central index and the trade mark register. No one-stop name reservation exists for a SARL; the proposed name must include 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or 'SARL' and be submitted for notarial drafting only after conflicts are excluded. A printed availability search is retained in the incorporation file.
required_dossiers: List of three proposed corporate names in order of preference
Trade mark search report (Luxembourg IP Office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is identical or confusingly similar to an existing RCS entry or protected trade mark, the founders select the next available name; no incorporation deed is signed until availability is confirmed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of blocked capital account and obtaining banker's certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution (e.g. Spuerkeess, BIL, BGL BNP Paribas)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders open a blocked account (compte bloqué) in the name of the SARL in formation and deposit the full minimum capital of EUR 12,000. The bank issues a certificate confirming that the funds are placed at the disposal of the company and frozen until the incorporation deed is executed.
required_dossiers: Identity documents of each shareholder and manager
KYC/AML forms and proof of source of funds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank declines on KYC grounds, an alternative Luxembourg credit institution may be engaged; the statutory timeline only starts once the banker's certificate is available for the notary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The founders appear before the notary to execute the acte constitutif. The notary verifies the share subscriptions, the banker's certificate for cash contributions, any in-kind valuation report, the manager's acceptance, and the registered office proof. Upon signature the company is constituted but does not yet have legal existence vis-à-vis third parties.
required_dossiers: Notarised powers of attorney for any absent shareholder
Valid identity documents of shareholders and managers
Final Articles of Association approved by the notary
Proof of registered office address (lease or letter of accommodation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The notary postpones signing until defects are cured, such as an insufficient capital certificate or missing power of attorney; corrections are made by deed amendment or addendum without losing the incorporation file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS inscription and electronic filing of incorporation deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS/LBR), via notary electronic transmission or physical lodgement
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The original notarial deed and the RCS filing application are lodged with the LBR. The filing contains the corporate details, registered office, object (digital advertising and media buying), share capital, and identity of the manager. Registration confers full legal personality.
required_dossiers: Banker's certificate of the blocked capital account
RCS registration form signed by the manager
Evidence of payment of state filing fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises an insuffisance or formal objection, counsel submits corrections and supplemental statements via the e-filing portal within the permitted delay; the registration is re-examined upon complete filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the RESA and verifiability against third parties
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following RCS inscription, the register automatically publishes in RESA. This publication gives the deed legal effect and opposability against third parties. The manager must verify the published excerpt for accuracy.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published extract contains an error, the manager applies to RCS for rectification with a notarial erratum. Publication delays beyond the statutory window may be chased administratively but do not invalidate the incorporation once published.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business establishment permit application for commercial activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy - Direction générale des PME, through guichet.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The SARL, as an entity carrying on a commercial activity in digital advertising and affiliate media buying, must hold an autorisation d'établissement under the Law of 2 September 2011. The legal manager submits the application in the company's name, proving absence of bankruptcy, professional integrity, and relevant professional competence. The permit is issued for the company and its registered office address.
required_dossiers: Criminal record certificate of the managing director
Pre-application social security acknowledgement where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of refusal, the company may file a fresh application with completed moralité or professional qualification evidence, or appeal to the Minister of the Economy within one month of notification of the refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT, social security, and beneficial ownership registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Luxembourg Business Registers for the RBE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS inscription and before operations launch, the SARL registers for Luxembourg VAT on advertising services, enrols the manager and staff with CCSS, and files the initial declaration of beneficial owners in the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) with the LBR. These filings activate the operative tax and employment framework for the media buying business.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT number issuance is delayed, the company may invoice with a VAT number pending confirmation, provided AEDT is informed. Late RBE filings attract fines but the administration accepts correcting declarations; the manager should use e-file tracking to evidence timely submission.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy - Direction générale des PME for the business establishment permit; Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity - Administration de l'environnement for environmental permitting of the operating premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) issued under the Law of 2 September 2011 governing access to commercial, craft, and industrial professions; applicable to the company's registered office and any permanent establishment used for digital advertising and affiliate media buying (ISIC 7310).

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Class 4 business-service activity; not listed in Annexes I or II of the Law of 15 May 2008 on environmental impact assessment; no full EIA report or formal screening certificate required for an office-based media buying operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office-only operation, therefore no industrial wastewater discharge; domestic sewage must comply with the municipal sewerage bylaws of the commune where the registered office is located. VOC and solvent use, if any limited ancillary printing or cleaning activity occurs, must respect the transposed EU Directive 2004/42/EC substance thresholds. Waste handling must comply with the Law of 21 March 2017 on waste, including segregated WEEE disposal for IT and media-buying equipment under Directive 2012/19/EU, and packaging waste recovery under the Law of 2 March 1998 as amended.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety clearance: the registered office fit-out must satisfy the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 9 December 1994 on fire safety, with a municipal fire safety certificate issued by the local commune. Structural load: the building owner's architectural calculation and lease structural load provisions certify category B office loading; any installation of server racks or heavy studio equipment above 2.5 kN/m² requires a structural engineer's verification. Occupational clearance: the occupier must declare the workplace to the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM), prepare a written risk assessment under the Law of 17 June 1994 transposing Directive 89/391/EEC, appoint a safety delegate when staffing thresholds are reached, and maintain first-aid and fire-exit arrangements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and indirect tax registration; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct tax; unified electronic portal: MyGuichet (myguichet.lu) and eTVA e-filing; business registry: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Luxembourg SARL obtains its national business identification number (numéro d'identification national) automatically upon incorporation and RCS registration. VAT identification number (format LU + 8 digits) is procured via the AEDT through the MyGuichet/eTVA portal by filing the commencement declaration. Non-resident entities without a Luxembourg establishment must appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative and file the same declaration, evidencing a local fiscal address or accredited representative; where no domestic taxable activity exists, reverse charge obviates local VAT registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (resident SARL subject to corporate income tax at the aggregate effective rate of 24.94% (CIT 17% plus surcharge and municipal business tax), net wealth tax at 0.5%, with worldwide income taxation subject to territorial exemptions; no pass-through treatment).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime; statutory elections available under Luxembourg law: (i) fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) election for CIT/municipal business tax among resident parent and 95%-owned subsidiaries; (ii) VAT grouping election (assujetti unique) for closely-linked resident entities; (iii) participation exemption election for 100% dividend exemption and 50% capital-gains exemption on qualifying shareholdings; (iv) IP box 80% exemption election for qualifying intellectual property income; hybrid mismatch adjustments apply mandatorily in accordance with ATAD.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic threshold for established taxable persons—registration is mandatory from the first taxable transaction. For non-established suppliers: EUR 10,000 EU-wide distance-selling threshold for B2C supplies of goods/e-services; B2B services to Luxembourg customers fall under reverse charge without local registration; physical importation of goods always triggers import VAT liability regardless of any threshold.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No national real-time clearance or continuous transaction control (CTC) mandate for B2B invoices; Peppol-based B2G e-invoicing (Factur-X/ZUGFeRD) is compulsory for supplies to Luxembourg public entities since April 2023; VAT returns (monthly or quarterly) must be filed electronically via MyGuichet/eTVA; invoices must carry mandatory sequential numbering and be archived digitally for 10 years.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to (i) physical exports of goods to destinations outside the EU where transport is completed and evidenced by customs export documentation; (ii) B2B services, including cross-border digital advertising/media-buying services, supplied to taxable customers established outside the EU—place of supply being outside Luxembourg; proof of the recipient's non-EU establishment and taxable-person status must be retained; customs export proof must be obtained within 90 days of the supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (electronic EU Single Administrative Document) with assigned MRN and confirmation of exit from the EU territory
Transport evidence: international waybill (CMR for road, Bill of Lading for sea, Airway Bill for air) covering the movement to the non-EU destination
Commercial invoice, underlying supply contract, and purchase order for the export transaction
Bank or payment documentation evidencing receipt of foreign currency (inward remittance certificate or SWIFT credit advice)

For offshore services: service agreement, recipient's foreign VAT registration or tax-identification certificate, and documentary evidence that the advertising/media-buying services are supplied to and enjoyed by the recipient outside Luxembourg
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEDT may claw back zero-rating and assess domestic 17% VAT plus late interest at 0.6% per month where export proof is absent, forged, untimely (over 90 days), or insufficient; culpable VAT fraud carries administrative fines of up to 100% of the tax evaded, criminal fines up to EUR 250,000, imprisonment up to 5 years (up to 10 years for organized fraud), potential publication of the conviction, and joint and several director liability; refunds linked to suspected fictitious exports are suspended pending forensic verification.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), acting within the Eurosystem and exercising delegated foreign exchange administration functions alongside the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for financial supervision; BCL is the depository for reserve statistics and external position reporting under EU regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg applies full liberalisation of capital movements and current payments under EU Treaty provisions (article 63 TFEU). No exchange control approval is required for cross-border dividends, interest, royalties, capital injections, or trade settlements. Profit remittance is unrestricted and free of local withholding on distributions once the participation exemption or ordinary treaty relief applies, subject only to anti-abuse (GAAR) and substance verification. Non-EU currency transactions are freely executed through authorised credit institutions with no mandatory conversion. Reporting obligations are limited to balance-of-payments statistical returns collected by BCL for the Eurosystem, not prior authorisations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion ratio for export proceeds exists in Luxembourg. Exporters may retain and use export receipts freely in EUR or foreign currency. No timeline is imposed for repatriation of proceeds, provided that invoicing and settlement are conducted through a Luxembourg credit institution for bankability and capital movement statistics. For affiliate media buying services, cross-border earned receipts are classified as service export proceeds and are treated identically to any other current account foreign claim.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with multi-currency and payment card sub-limits

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating is Medium-Risk with legal constraints. Luxembourg does not grant domestic EMI authorisation; a fintech EMI must hold a PSD2 authorisation from another EEA member state and passport into Luxembourg via the notification regime. Such EMIs may support EUR IBANs and SWIFT/SEPA clearing but generally do not offer escrow or recorded capital account structures. Their use as principal treasury bank is discouraged; viable only as a secondary disbursement rail. Non-EU/offshore digital EMIs are not permitted to operate as deposit-takers or to provide payment accounts to Luxembourg entities, because they lack an EEA passport; any use is legally constrained to unregulated prepaid instruments, which are unsuitable for corporate treasury.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Traditional tier-one Luxembourg banks generally require at least one physical appearance of an authorised director or the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) before account opening; remote opening is possible but conditioned on relationship managers at the bank venue in Luxembourg, notarised identification documents (if required by bank policy), and apostilised corporate records for non-EU shareholders. A pure virtual opening without any in-person visit is only offered by selected digital banking units and EEA passported EMIs, subject to strict video-KYC and corroboration of corporate documents. For a SARL engaged in media buying, a physical presence of the managing director, or a mandatory interview by a bank officer acting under a power-of-attorney, is the industry-standard onboarding path to avoid account refusal.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undefined or unnecessary corporate structure for affiliate media buying: multiple cross-border intermediate entities without transparent commercial rationale
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Group organisational chart, shareholder register (RBE/UBO register), contract chain for media buying, detailed commercial substance explanation, business plan with forecasted counterparties, and documentary evidence that the Luxembourg SARL serves as principal or risk-taker rather than a pass-through.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume outbound payments to ad networks, affiliate platforms, or data/media vendors in high-risk or sanctions-adjacent jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supplier agreements, master service agreements (ISSA or equivalent), invoice register with campaign IDs, complete KYC package for each vendor, jurisdictional risk assessment, media buying policy, and UBO-beneficial ownership declarations of the payment recipients.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent source-of-funds information for the initial capital injection from non-EU shareholders
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank-source letters, certified share capital transfer receipts, audited financial statements of foreign shareholders, legal opinion on funds origination, tax clearance certificate, evidence of dividend or salary accumulation, and no-discrepancy declaration supporting the exact capital amount.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Pending or unexplained director/UBO sanctions exposure or politically exposed person (PEP) status
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent global sanctions screening report, PEP self-declaration with mitigating explanation, sworn justification of commercial relationship, article of incorporation excerpt showing board approval, AML manuals, CV and identity documents of the PEP or UBO, and confirmation of no direct exposure to restricted regime.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 to the Luxembourg operational account with purpose code CAPT (capital contribution) or CHGD (payment of charges) as required by the receiving bank; in SEPA zone, provide EUR transfer with explicit remittance information 'Capital contribution — LU SARL <entity ref>'. BCL balance-of-payments reporting requires that transfers exceeding EUR 12,500 attributable to direct investment be flagged as FDI. Verification must include notarial deed of transfer, updated RBE/UBO database extract, bank confirmation letter, and statutory manager’s minute approving the issuance of new shares or contribution to capital reserves.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: SEPA Instant/Credit Transfer for EU/EEC vendors using primary bank rails; SWIFT MT103 for non-EU vendor payments referencing underlying invoices and service description. For large settlement of media buying inventory, a commercial letter of credit (UCP600) via SWIFT MT700/MT799 with performance or payment guarantee can be used, but the dominant clearing rail is bank-to-bank wire. Digital EMI accounts (Wise, Mercury) can be used only as ancillary rails for low-value facilitation, never as principal treasury repositories. Additionally, card-based rails (Visa/Mastercard corporate cards) can process ad-network charges up to bank-set limits.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Interest rate swaps collateralised under EMIR

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts (balance sheet, P&L, notes, and auditor's report if applicable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL), administered by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December year-end, the annual accounts must be approved by the general meeting no later than 30 June of the following year and lodged with the RCSL within one month of approval, i.e. no later than 31 July.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing exposes the managers to administrative and criminal penalties; the RCSL registrar may issue a compliance summons, and if annual accounts remain unfiled for two consecutive financial years, the competent authority may request judicial dissolution and strike-off from the RCSL with loss of legal personality.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial ownership information (confirmation annuelle RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually no later than 31 March of each calendar year, irrespective of the financial year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or confirm beneficial ownership information, or knowingly filing false information, is a criminal offence subject to fines and imprisonment under the Luxembourg RBE Law; the competent authorities may also initiate corrective enforcement proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual consolidated tax return for corporate income tax (CIT), municipal business tax (MBT), and net wealth tax (NWT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December year-end, the consolidated annual tax return is due on 31 December of the following year, subject to duly authorised extensions and e-filing practices.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing allows the tax administration to proceed with ex officio assessment, levy default interest and late-payment or late-filing surcharges, and pursue enforcement; directors/managers may be held personally liable in cases of fraudulent or unlawful dissipation of corporate assets.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Luxembourg SARL must appoint an independent accredited auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) when it exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds for two consecutive financial years: balance-sheet total EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average number of employees 50. Additionally, regulated activities and certain parent companies are always subject to statutory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Statutory annual accounts must be prepared in accordance with Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2008 on commercial companies and annual accounts; IFRS is permitted only in specific consolidated or listed-group contexts.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Before 31 March of each year, the SARL must review and confirm through the RBE that the recorded beneficial ownership information remains accurate. Any share transfer or change of effective ownership or control must be declared to the RBE within one month of the event, in addition to the mandatory annual confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (registre des parts sociales)
Minute Book of shareholder and management meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,200–3,000 per annum for registered office and resident corporate officer/agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000–20,000 per annum for a small SARL statutory audit engagement

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (combined CIT 17% + solidarity surcharge 7% + municipal business tax ~6.75% for first €175,000; progressive top marginal rate 40.455%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced rate of 18.19% (CIT 17% + solidarity surcharge) on first €175,000 taxable income; participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains; IP box regime (80% exemption on qualifying IP income) subject to substance requirements; notional interest deduction on new equity capital.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 1000 (Corporate Income Tax Return) filed via eC (electronic filing) on MyGuichet.lu; municipal business tax return (Form 1002) and net wealth tax return (Form 1003) filed simultaneously.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing deadline is 31 months after the end of the fiscal year (e.g., for FY ending 31 Dec 2024, due 31 July 2027). Extensions are possible upon request.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income (net profit before tax adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Luxembourg-source income only; non-resident companies are taxed on Luxembourg-source income unless a PE exists.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions for participation exemption (dividends and capital gains)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim only if holding ≥10% or acquisition cost ≥€1.2 million and held for at least 12 months; non-residents must meet same conditions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net wealth tax (calculated on net assets)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents are subject to net wealth tax only on Luxembourg-situs assets (e.g., real estate, PE assets).
Disclose any adjustments to align with arm's length principle; non-residents must maintain TP documentation if related party transactions exceed thresholds.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: 10% of tax due (minimum €250). Interest on late payment: 0.6% per month (7.2% p.a.). Additional penalties for gross negligence or fraud up to 100% of tax due.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (reduced to 0% under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if parent holds ≥10% for ≥12 months; treaty rates may apply)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim treaty relief, submit a Luxembourg tax residence certificate (TRC) and the relevant treaty article to the paying agent. For reduced WHT, file a request for exemption (form 105) with the Luxembourg tax authorities before payment. For foreign tax credit, include the TRC and proof of tax paid in the annual return.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: royalties 15%, interest 15%. Treaty rates typically 0-10% for royalties and 0-10% for interest depending on the treaty. EU Interest & Royalty Directive may reduce to 0% if beneficial ownership and 25% shareholding conditions met.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required if related party transactions exceed €450,000 per year; Master File required if consolidated group revenue exceeds €12 million (EU threshold) or €50 million (Luxembourg threshold).
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) for entities engaged in IP, financing, and holding activities. For a media buying company, substance is assessed based on: (i) physical presence (office, staff), (ii) strategic decision-making in Luxembourg, (iii) adequate IT infrastructure, and (iv) operational control. Failure to demonstrate substance may lead to reclassification of income and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of income, false invoicing, or concealment of related-party transactions to reduce taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal fine up to €250,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years; civil penalty of 100% of tax evaded plus interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held personally liable for tax debts if they knowingly participated in evasion; travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating as a letterbox company with no real office, employees, or decision-making in Luxembourg, while claiming tax benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of tax treaty benefits, reclassification of income, and penalty of up to 10% of turnover. Under EU ATAD, substance requirements are mandatory.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be liable for unpaid taxes if they failed to ensure substance; potential criminal charges for fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct adequate customer due diligence, suspicious transaction reporting, or maintaining anonymous accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to €5 million or 10% of annual turnover; criminal penalties for money laundering up to 5 years imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally fined and imprisoned; professional disqualification and travel restrictions may apply.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to maintain TP documentation or applying non-arm's length pricing on related-party transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Adjustment of taxable income, penalty of 10% of the adjustment, and interest on underpaid tax. In severe cases, criminal penalties for tax evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be personally liable for penalties if they approved the non-compliant pricing; potential criminal liability for fraudulent misrepresentation.
